name: UK

flag.title: The Union Jack
flag.note: Red, white & blue cross of three nations

lead: The UK is four countries: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Shakespeare, the steam engine, the Web and football all came from here. Once it ruled a quarter of the Earth.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The UK covers Great Britain and the north of Ireland. The Channel, just 34 km wide at its narrowest, separates it from Europe. Scotland's Highlands have lochs (lakes) and craggy mountains.
Wales has green valleys. The coastline stretches over 17,800 km. No point in England is more than 113 km from the sea.
animals: The red squirrel is Britain's native squirrel. It is now rare because the larger grey squirrel arrived from America in 1876. Puffins nest on rocky sea cliffs each spring.
The robin is Britain's unofficial national bird. It is bold enough to perch on a gardener's spade. Wild Dartmoor ponies roam the southwest moors.
culture: The British love a queue. Standing in an orderly line is almost a national sport. People brew tea over 100 million times every day.
The BBC began in 1927 and is the world's oldest national broadcaster. Bonfire Night on 5 November fills the sky with fireworks.
history: Romans invaded in 43 AD. They built roads and baths. The Normans arrived in 1066, the last successful invasion. Magna Carta in 1215 planted the seed of modern democracy.
The Industrial Revolution began here in the 1760s. By the 1920s the British Empire was the largest in history. In 1948 Britain created the NHS, which gives free healthcare.
wows: London's Underground opened in 1863 as the world's first metro.
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web and gave it away free.
Britain has no single written constitution and runs on centuries-old laws.
The UK enters four separate teams in World Cup qualifying.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire began.
Only the United States has had more Nobel Prize winners than the UK.
Big Ben is only the bell, and the tower is the Elizabeth Tower.

myths.myth: It rains every single day in Britain
myths.fact: London gets less rain each year than Rome or Miami. It drizzles often, but rarely pours.
Parliament and the Prime Minister make the real decisions. The King's job is mostly ceremonial (for show).
